📖 Core Definitions

Essential Terminology & Concepts

Timeliness Core Definition

Timeliness how current and up-to-date the information is.

Reliability Core Definition

Reliability data accuracy, across the several sources and systems.

Properties Of Data Key Concept

The effectiveness of data-backed decision- making primarily depends on the quality of the data.

Datafication Key Concept

Organizations have acknowledged the power of informed, data-backed decisions for their operations.

Data Format Key Concept

Two types of data are possible: quantitative and qualitative.

📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

2.2 Properties of Data

  • The effectiveness of data-backed decision- making primarily depends on the quality of the data.
  • Inadequate data quality might result in inferior decision- making and unnecessary expenditures or possible business losses.
  • Evaluating and improving data quality is essential for the successful execution of data science projects and the overall performance of the organization.
  • The following aspects of data are crucial in assessing data quality.

2.3 Datafication

  • Organizations have acknowledged the power of informed, data-backed decisions for their operations.
  • The effectiveness of data-backed decision- making primarily depends on the quality of the data.
  • Inadequate data quality might result in inferior decision- making and unnecessary expenditures or possible business losses.
  • Evaluating and improving data quality is essential for the successful execution of data science projects and the overall performance of the organization.

2.4 Data Categories: Qualitative & Quantitative Data

  • Data science sees every activity in the form of data.
  • It essentially converts everything we do into data.
  • This process of converting various aspects of our lives into data is called datafication.
  • Datafication is then used to draw insights, make predictions, and improve various aspects of life and business.

2.5 Data Format

  • Two types of data are possible: quantitative and qualitative.
  • It's important to know the difference between the two because they need different ways to collect and analyse data.
  • Quantitative data implies the data which can be measured or counted and expressed in the form of numerical values.
  • Accordingly, it gives us Introduction to Data Science-1 62 information about “how many,” “how much,” or “how often”.

2.5.1 Structured Data

  • Establishes essential concepts, mathematical or computational foundations, and techniques of structured data.
  • Applies standard methodologies relevant to modern data science workflows and analysis in understanding data and its type.

2.5.2 Unstructured Data

  • Establishes essential concepts, mathematical or computational foundations, and techniques of unstructured data.
  • Applies standard methodologies relevant to modern data science workflows and analysis in understanding data and its type.

2.5.3 Semi-structured Data

  • Establishes essential concepts, mathematical or computational foundations, and techniques of semi-structured data.
  • Applies standard methodologies relevant to modern data science workflows and analysis in understanding data and its type.

2.6 Primary Data & Secondary Data

  • The data format defines the structure of data within a system be it database/filebase system, imparting relevance to the processed data i.e.
  • Sources of the data may exist in various formats.
  • The following three formats are often utilized.
  • Structured data is typically characterised by rows and columns, with columns denoting various attributes/elements such as emp_name, emp_ address, and emp_phone number, each field possessing a certain type, including various data types viz.
